name: Sishwala
subtitle: Sishwala is a traditional Swazi dish of maize and beans.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: A traditional Swazi porridge, listed among the country's most popular dishes.

facts.label: Main ingredients
facts.value: Dried sugar beans, maize flour, water and salt.

facts.label: Variation
facts.value: A Swazi food-security study describes sishwala as boiled maize with jugo beans, a maize-and-legume snack food.

facts.label: Context
facts.value: Much of the population lives on a diet of sorghum and maize.

parts.text: Sishwala is a traditional Swazi dish of maize and beans. A press account describes it as a porridge of dried sugar beans, maize flour, water and salt; a University of the Free State dissertation describes it as boiled maize and jugo beans. It belongs to a diet built largely on maize and sorghum.

gaps: The description is summarised from the sources listed here and should be read against them.

Not found in a readable source: Only two acceptable sources were found, and they disagree on the form (porridge vs. boiled maize and jugo beans as a snack). No source stating how or when it is eaten passed verification, and no complete recipe was found.
